name: ducking
about: Sidechain ducking maths (cpl/dsp.py): level key, reduction curve, attack/release smoothing and the multiplier applied to the background.

scenario.input: every 10 ms window holds ONE constant sample value per channel

duck_key._info: RMS (0..1) of the louder channel per 10 ms window of 48 kHz stereo 16-bit; the input is, per 10 ms: 5 silent, 10 at (16384, 8192), 5 at (3277, 0), 5 silent, 3 at (1000, 16384)

scenario.input: the key of the duck_key case (same windows) is passed to duck_curve with each row's level, ratio, threshold_db and hold

duck_curve._info_tolerance: case-level tolerance (dB), overrides the file's 2e-6: the Python key is float32 and carries about 1e-6 relative noise on the (3277, 0) windows, which moves the reduction by up to about 1.2e-5 dB
duck_curve._info: dB of reduction wanted per 10 ms before smoothing: max(0, dB(key*level) - threshold) * (1 - 1/ratio), capped at 60 dB; hold keeps the 75th-percentile depth from the first to the last active window

scenario.input: duck_curve(key, level, ratio, threshold_db, hold) with the key of this signal

duck_curve_hold_percentile._info: hold = true keeps the 75th-percentile depth (of the windows above 0.05 dB) from the first to the last active window. The ramp has targets from 0 to about 25 dB, so the depth is clearly different for the 60th and the 90th percentile.

scenario.input: each row: attack_ms, release_ms and the target series (segments = runs of equal target, `steps` long); dsp.duck_smooth is applied once per 10 ms step

duck_smooth._info: one step per 10 ms: gr += (tgt - gr) * (1 - exp(-dt/tau)); tau = attack when tgt > gr else release (min 1 ms); snaps to 0 when tgt == 0 and gr < 0.05

background_gain._info: the background deck volume is multiplied by 10^(-gr/20) (Deck.duck)

scenario.input: each row: rms (0..1), gain_db, ratio, threshold_db

input_target_db._info: Live input detector: the same gain computation as duck_curve (hold off), with its own threshold

duck_loop._info_tolerance_by_key: bg_multiplier (measured) is compared at 6e-4: Python only rewrites Deck.duck when it moved by more than 0.0005 (quirk 9), so it trails ideal_bg_multiplier = 10^(-gr_db/20) of the same row by up to 5e-4. The CONTRACT is ideal_bg_multiplier (file tolerance 2e-6)
duck_loop._info: the REAL _duck_loop and Play on Top under the fake clock: background deck + a 2 s voice-over (0.3 s silence, 0.7 s at 16384, 0.5 s at 4096, 0.5 s silence, stereo 48 kHz), sampled every 10 ms from 0.5 s before the voice-over until after the release. target_db = the duck_curve value the loop reads at top_pos + 20 ms (look-ahead); gr_db = smoothed reduction; bg_multiplier = Deck.duck of the background (applied only when it moved by more than 0.0005, so it can trail 10^(-gr/20) by that). Index 49 is the last background-only sample (t = 0.5 s, voice-over not started), index 50 is the voice-over starting at the same time (top_pos 0); from index 51 every row is 10 ms later, with the reduction computed by the loop at that time.

scenario.see: the `scenario` of the duck_loop case, plus `settings` here

voice_phase_2_5ms._info: the voice-over starts 12.5 ms after a 10 ms step of the control grid: phase 2.5 ms. The loop's first turn runs 2.5 ms after the voice-over started, so every step reads the playhead at 10 + 2.5 + 10 k ms. The look-ahead position is floor(playhead / 10 ms) + 2 (see _info_look_ahead_rule): at a phase of 0.25 step floor and round agree and only ceil differs
voice_phase_2_5ms._info_look_ahead_rule: the loop reads `curve[int((playhead - origin) / 0.01) + 2]`, i.e. FLOOR of the playhead in 10 ms windows plus 2. Replaying the recorded playheads and curves through duck_smooth reproduces gr_db for floor and for no other rounding; rows of gr_db that the other roundings would change: {"floor": 0, "round": 0, "ceil": 347}

voice_phase_7ms._info: phase 7 ms (a start at 17 ms): the playhead is 10 + 7 + 10 k ms at every step; floor takes the window the playhead is in, round and ceil the next one: rows where the curve changes between two windows differ
voice_phase_7ms._info_look_ahead_rule: the loop reads `curve[int((playhead - origin) / 0.01) + 2]`, i.e. FLOOR of the playhead in 10 ms windows plus 2. Replaying the recorded playheads and curves through duck_smooth reproduces gr_db for floor and for no other rounding; rows of gr_db that the other roundings would change: {"floor": 0, "round": 347, "ceil": 347}

voice_phase_9_9ms._info: phase 9.9 ms (a start at 9.9 ms, just before a step): the playhead is 10 + 9.9 + 10 k ms, almost a whole step past a window; floor still takes the window it is in, round and ceil the next one
voice_phase_9_9ms._info_look_ahead_rule: the loop reads `curve[int((playhead - origin) / 0.01) + 2]`, i.e. FLOOR of the playhead in 10 ms windows plus 2. Replaying the recorded playheads and curves through duck_smooth reproduces gr_db for floor and for no other rounding; rows of gr_db that the other roundings would change: {"floor": 0, "round": 347, "ceil": 347}

second_voice_over.started_by: play_on_top while the first is ducking

second_voice_starts_off_grid_while_ducki._info: a second voice-over (the same 2 s file) is played on top 2.5 ms after step 60, while the first is ducking (0.6 s into it, loud part). The FIRST voice-over is superseded: it fades out over top_fade_ms (1.5 s, not shown) and stops driving the ducking. The loop is NOT restarted (one loop task for the whole run: `ducking_loop_tasks`), its 10 ms timer goes on, so the second voice-over's playhead at its first step is 7.5 ms (off the voice's own grid) and then 17.5, 27.5 ... ms. gr_db is NOT reset: the smoothing carries on from the depth the first voice-over had reached (19.98 dB) towards the new voice-over's curve, read from ITS playhead (origin 0). The new voice-over starts with 0.3 s of silence, so the depth relaxes at the release rate for those 0.3 s and then follows the new voice-over: no jump up or down at the replacement. `top_n` says which voice-over drives the ducking. Contract: the continuity of gr_db and the curve of the new voice-over; not contract: the 7.5 ms phase of its steps (quirk 16)
second_voice_starts_off_grid_while_ducki._info_look_ahead_rule: floor, as in voice_phase_*: rows the other roundings would change: {"floor": 0, "round": 362, "ceil": 362}

second_voice_over.started_by: play_on_top while the first is ducking

second_voice_ends_first._info: a shorter second voice-over (1 s) starts on the grid 0.55 s into the first and is over (1.55 s into the first) before the first would have ended (2.0 s). The first is superseded at once, so when the SECOND ends the ducking releases (500 ms) although the first is still fading out for another half second: the first no longer counts. One loop task throughout (the end of the second voice-over is found by the 50 ms tick, quirk 6: row 160). Contract: the release starts when the SECOND ends (the first, superseded, no longer drives the ducking: `superseded` decks are skipped when a top voice-over ends); not contract: the phase of the steps (quirk 16)
second_voice_ends_first._info_look_ahead_rule: floor: rows the other roundings would change: {"floor": 0, "round": 315, "ceil": 315}
